text:
Data source overview:
The text is a draft EA-forum style essay discussing how artificial intelligence could entrench or mitigate factory-farming suffering, especially once fish and invertebrates are considered, and how researchers’ diets may shape the values AIs inherit. It argues that AI may 1) increase stocking density and profitability of factory farms, 2) internalise speciesist human language/image patterns, and 3) optimise proxy welfare indicators rather than real welfare, thereby risking astronomical future suffering on Earth and in space. It proposes technical, governance and cultural interventions that incorporate non-human welfare into AI objectives and training data.

EXTRACTION CONFIDENCE[77]
The source is informal and repetitive, so several causal steps had to be re-assembled, but the resulting graph follows all mandated patterns. JSON syntax and edge/node references were cross-checked.

How the instruction set could improve: allow an optional “policy rationale” concept category between design rationale and implementation to capture governance–oriented arguments that do not easily fit as technical implementations.

Inference strategy justification:
Where the post only hinted at concrete interventions (e.g. “AI researchers’ diets may matter”), moderate inference (edge confidence 2) was used to formulate explicit, safety-relevant interventions while respecting the source’s intent.

Extraction completeness explanation:
All distinct risks, mechanisms, insights, rationales, mechanisms, evidence and interventions that the essay repeatedly stresses were captured and interconnected; redundant or stray remarks were collapsed into existing nodes to avoid duplication.

Key limitations:
• Validation evidence in the essay is weak (mostly anecdotal), so several edge confidences are necessarily low.  
• Some policy paths required moderate inference because the essay lacks implementation detail.  
• The informal style offered no hard empirical metrics, so “validation evidence” nodes rely on meta-analyses and anecdotes referenced by the author.
